locator: I-II q.91 a.2 s.c. and co., lumen rationis naturalis, quo discernimus quid sit bonum et malum
interpretation: I-II q.91 a.2 s.c.: on Rom 2:14 the Gloss says 'etsi non habent legem scriptam, habent tamen legem naturalem, qua quilibet intelligit et sibi conscius est quid sit bonum et quid malum'; co.: 'lumen rationis naturalis, quo discernimus quid sit bonum et malum, quod pertinet ad naturalem legem, nihil aliud sit quam impressio divini luminis in nobis'. About practical reason (good and evil), not knowledge of God's existence.
attribution: The passage states that the light of natural reason, by which we discern good and evil, is an impression of the divine light in us, and, with the Gloss on Rom 2:14, that the gentiles without the written law have the natural law by which each understands what is good and evil, which is the premise.
